g1-implement.title: Assembly seam: the manifest becomes a byproduct of starting a step
g1-implement.imperative: Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md and dispatch constellation-implementer. THE CHANGE: emit the #300 context manifest from checklist_engine.start() and reopen() — the two and only two sites that set status 'in-progress' (:1635, :1852), which advance() at :1644 requires. That is what makes emission unskippable WITHOUT touching the shared dispatch() chokepoint. Write-if-absent, never overwrite: the manifest is a per-step delivery snapshot, and rewriting it on later verbs would destroy the record it exists to be. All logic lives in a NEW module scripts/episode_capture.py; the engine gains an import and one call per site. Roots resolved mechanically, no CLI flag: 'repo' from the worktree root; 'durable' from agent_work_root.durable_root() — the CHECKOUT root, NOT durable_agent_work(), because the one shipped declaration is {root: durable, path: .agent-work/LESSONS.md} and the wrong helper double-nests it to .agent-work/.agent-work/LESSONS.md; 'skill' from the installed skill dir. FAIL-SOFT BUT NOT SILENT: the emit must never change any verb's exit code (build_manifest() legitimately raises ValueError on a terminal checklist, and a crash here breaks every verb for every concurrent commander) — but a failed emit writes a stub manifest recording the failure. A non-reading must be visibly distinct from an uncollected one; a vanished manifest is forbidden. Wait for and integrate the returned IMPLEMENTER_RESULT.

g2-implement.imperative: Fill the handoff and dispatch constellation-implementer. THE CHANGE: a composer that fills the frozen mechanical field group from engine state with zero agent effort, emitted as a snapshot at the SAME seam as g1 so a run where the agent records nothing still yields the full group. Field sourcing is ADJUDICATED, not the implementer's choice: run=cl['work_id']; project=the MAIN CHECKOUT's name via durable_root(), NOT Path(worktree).name which yields 'e298-305' and would give the same repo a different project every epic; role=the lease's claimed_by; spine-step=active_id(cl), the one selector, imported never re-derived; context-manifest-ref='ctx-<work-id>-<step>@<rev>' where rev is context_manifest.rev() over the manifest's own bytes — this satisfies EPISODE_STORE.md:679-689's <manifest-ref>@<revision> contract verbatim ('pinning to its own blob hash at capture time') and is why g1's write-if-absent is load-bearing; rework-count from task['rework_count']; reopens from the journal's reopen entries; failed-commands from evidence type command-output with payload.exit != 0 — these survive a refusal because the evidence item is appended BEFORE the raise and main() persists on the error path; artifact-ref from _collect_changed_files() (:607), which already returns REPO-RELATIVE paths matching the shipped episodes' shape — do NOT invent an 'artifact-ref' evidence type, it has zero occurrences across ~900 evidence items and would be a second secretly-agent-dependent field. REFUSALS: pending the Admiral's ruling on float #1. If ruled in scope, increment a counter on main()'s except EngineError path, which already calls save(). If ruled out, the composer REFUSES rather than emitting a silent 0 — a 0 on a run that was actually refused is a fabricated mechanical fact, worse than an absent one. g3-implement.title: Negative control, proof it can fail, and cross-run retrieval
g3-implement.imperative: Fill the handoff and dispatch constellation-implementer. THE CONTROL: drive a real spine where the agent records NOTHING beyond what postconditions mechanically require, then assert the full mechanical field group is present AND CORRECT. Correctness is asserted against an INDEPENDENTLY-TALLIED GROUND TRUTH — the harness records each induced event at the moment it issues the triggering call, then compares field by field. DO NOT use apply_episode_delta.validate_delta() as the oracle: it is type-and-presence only (isinstance(str) and value.strip() for every string field), so a composer returning nine hardcoded constants passes it, and so does the delete-one-field red-proof, because deleting a key from a dict is independent of how the dict was filled. That control proves the validator rejects incomplete input, never that capture works. The validator stays in the pipeline as a shape check on the way to the writer; it is not the oracle. PROOF THE CONTROL CAN FAIL: run it against a deliberately incomplete capture — revert the composer to constants, or drop one derivation — and confirm it goes RED, asserting the SPECIFIC failed field, not merely non-zero exit. A wrapper that maps any non-zero to red also reports red for an import error or a collection failure; assert the specific assertion. Then CROSS-RUN RETRIEVAL: seed episodes, mark one cluster consolidated, confirm rhyme-search still finds its neighbours, and DISCARD the synthetic consolidation — a test artifact must never become canon; confirm the discard by normalized content or blob OID, never raw working-tree bytes (#319). Wait for and integrate IMPLEMENTER_RESULT.

constraints: A check that cannot fail is indistinguishable from one that passed. Prove you read BOTH things, then compare — empty-vs-empty, missing-vs-missing and skipped-vs-skipped all pass a naive equality check.
The red-proof must assert the SPECIFIC failure, not non-zero exit: import errors, collection errors and empty test selection all exit non-zero.
Comparisons use normalized content or blob OIDs, never raw working-tree bytes — episode bytes differ across worktrees under core.autocrlf (#319).
The synthetic consolidation is THROWAWAY and must be discarded, verified. The real first consolidation is #308.
HONEST NULL: if the control legitimately fails, that is this issue's most valuable output. Report which fields are secretly agent-dependent. Do NOT engineer around it.

g4-implement.title: Drop run.dirty (#327) and record the sequencing on main
g4-implement.imperative: Fill the handoff and dispatch constellation-implementer. THE CHANGE: remove run.dirty from context_manifest.py — removal, not repair, per a settled/human ruling. Per-declared-file dirtiness stays derivable from content alone (each row's rev vs git rev-parse <commit>:<path>), which is strictly better because it is scoped to the declared set. Drop the parameter from run_facts(), stop build_manifest() reading state.get('dirty'), update the ~25 assertion sites in tests/test_context_manifest.py, and correct the module docstring prose — stale prose describing a removed field is worse than no prose. CONTENT_KEYS is unchanged: dirty was never content. ALSO: add a successor line to #300's shipped design doc so a reader of main can tell deliberate sequencing from oversight — the producer had no caller until #305 wired it. Close #327 with the removal. Wait for and integrate IMPLEMENTER_RESULT.
